slot.subtopic: Structure of oxides of phosphorus / hydrolysis of PCl3-type halides
slot.brief: Predict hydrolysis products of a p-block trichloride/pentachloride with balanced equation and structural reasoning (why PCl5 gives two anions in solution) — hard mixed concept.

stem: On complete hydrolysis, which option gives the balanced equations for $\text{PCl}_3$ and $\text{PCl}_5$, plus the anions from the $\text{PCl}_5$ hydrolysate after the first ionisation of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$?

verdicts.working: PCl₃ hydrolysis gives H₃PO₃ + 3HCl; PCl₅ hydrolysis gives H₃PO₄ + 5HCl. The first ionisation of H₃PO₄ produces H₂PO₄⁻, alongside Cl⁻.

working:
$\text{PCl}_3+3\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3+3\text{HCl}$; $\text{PCl}_5+4\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4+5\text{HCl}$. $\text{HCl}\rightarrow\text{H}^++\text{Cl}^-$; $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4\rightleftharpoons\text{H}^++\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$.

Independent check: PCl₃ hydrolysis gives H₃PO₃ + 3HCl; PCl₅ hydrolysis gives H₃PO₄ + 5HCl. The first ionisation of H₃PO₄ produces H₂PO₄⁻, alongside Cl⁻.
solution: Hydrolysis gives $\text{PCl}_3+3\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3+3\text{HCl}$ and $\text{PCl}_5+4\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4+5\text{HCl}$. After the first ionisation, $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4\rightleftharpoons\text{H}^++\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$, while HCl gives $\text{Cl}^-$; hence the anions are $\text{Cl}^-$ and $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$.

draft.distractor_notes: B: Gives the wrong oxyacid for P(III); C: Uses complete deprotonation rather than the first ionisation of phosphoric acid; D: Does not conserve chlorine in the $\text{PCl}_5$ equation.
